pageTitle: Using service-linked roles for AWS WAF Classic
whatThePageStates: This is mostly a concept and how-to page about the two AWS WAF Classic service-linked roles, AWSServiceRoleForWAFLogging and AWSServiceRoleForWAFRegionalLogging. It explains what a service-linked role is, which trusted service principals assume each role, which IAM actions the attached permissions policies allow (firehose:PutRecord, firehose:PutRecordBatch, kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:Decrypt), and how the roles are created, edited and deleted. The only coverage statement on the page is the final section 'Supported Regions for AWS WAF Classic service-linked roles', a three-column table listing 16 AWS Regions, every one marked Yes in the 'Support in AWS WAF Classic' column. There are no No or Partial entries, and the page carries an end-of-life warning for AWS WAF Classic plus a note steering readers to current AWS WAF.

features.featureName: Supported Regions for AWS WAF Classic service-linked roles
features.statuses: 16 Yes, 0 No, 0 Partial; 16+0+0=16. Every data row of the table has the literal value 'Yes' in the third column, 'Support in AWS WAF Classic'. The table has 18 pipe-delimited lines: 1 header, 1 separator, 16 data rows. No row states non-support, and there is no exclusion sentence elsewhere on the page, so this page makes no not-supported claim about any Region. The 16 Region identities are us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-1, us-west-2, ap-south-1, ap-northeast-3, ap-northeast-2, ap-southeast-1, ap-southeast-2, ap-northeast-1, ca-central-1, eu-central-1, eu-west-1, eu-west-2, eu-west-3, sa-east-1.
features.scope: None as a second enumerated dimension. The table is a single flat list with no per-plan, per-scan-method or per-role column. The two service-linked roles (AWSServiceRoleForWAFLogging and AWSServiceRoleForWAFRegionalLogging) are named in an earlier section but the Region table does not split by role — its header says 'Support in AWS WAF Classic' and its section title says 'service-linked roles' plural, so all 16 Yes values apply to the roles collectively, not per role. Reading a 2x16 grid out of this page would be inventing a dimension the page does not state.
features.reasoning: The axis is region because the enumerated thing is the AWS Region universe, which exists independently of AWS WAF Classic, and each row names one Region by name and identity. The unit of claim is one Region equals one value: each row is a self-contained assertion that service-linked roles for AWS WAF Classic are supported there. Rows do not collapse — 16 rows name 16 distinct Region identities with no duplicates — so distinctTargets and collapse are omitted.

shouldNotExtract: The two service-linked role names (AWSServiceRoleForWAFLogging, AWSServiceRoleForWAFRegionalLogging) are an inventory of roles, not a coverage claim, and must not be counted as a two-value axis. The trusted service principals (waf.amazonaws.com, waf-regional.amazonaws.com) are trust-policy detail. The IAM actions in the permissions policies (firehose:PutRecord, firehose:PutRecordBatch, kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:Decrypt) are policy contents, not an apiOperation coverage catalogue — the page does not claim these are all the operations AWS WAF Classic supports. The iam:CreateServiceLinkedRole prerequisite, the numbered delete walkthrough steps, the console/CLI/API instructions, the end-of-life Warning, the AWS WAF Classic version Note, the 'Introducing a new console experience' banner, the outbound links to the IAM User Guide and 'AWS Services That Work with IAM', and the 'See also' AI-coding-assistant Agent Toolkit boilerplate are all non-coverage. The phrase 'look for the services that have Yes in the Service-Linked Role column' refers to a table on a DIFFERENT page and must not be harvested here.
coverageDimensions: REGION: this page gives 16 Regions, all supported (Yes), for AWS WAF Classic service-linked roles. That is the page's only quantitative coverage statement. SERVICE: nothing. The page is about one service (AWS WAF Classic) and does not enumerate services; the mentions of Amazon Data Firehose, AWS KMS and IAM are dependency and policy detail, not a per-service support matrix, and any 'N services supported' figure from this page is fabricated. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing. The page names no resource-type list; web ACLs and Firehose delivery streams appear only inside instructions and policy conditions, so any resource-type count from this page is fabricated.
trap: The single most likely misparse is treating the two service-linked role names as a coverage axis and reporting 2 supported items, or multiplying them against the 16 Regions to claim 32 — the page never splits Region support per role. Runner-up: harvesting the four IAM actions (firehose:PutRecord, firehose:PutRecordBatch, kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:Decrypt) as an apiOperation coverage catalogue when they are just the contents of a permissions policy. Runner-up: a naive regex for 'No' in the table matching the substring inside 'Asia Pacific (Osaka) | ap-northeast-3', 'Seoul | ap-northeast-2' and 'Tokyo | ap-northeast-1', producing a phantom 3 No entries when all 16 rows are Yes. Runner-up: counting the table's header and separator lines as data, yielding 17 or 18 instead of 16. Runner-up: reading the sentence about the 'Service-Linked Role column' with 'Yes' entries as a claim made by THIS page, when it points at the IAM services page. Final runner-up: inferring from the end-of-life Warning that support is No or Partial — the page states Yes for all 16 Regions regardless of the deprecation notice.
